claims.text: A partially recrystallized heterogeneous grain structure can simultaneously enhance yield strength and tensile ductility in a multi-principal element alloy.
The simultaneous strength and ductility enhancement arises from back-stress hardening together with deformation twinning in coarse grains.
Fully recrystallized ultrafine-grained or coarse-grained CrCoNi- or FeCoCrNi-based alloys typically suffer from brittleness or a strength-ductility trade-off at room temperature.
A cold-rolling reduction of approximately 75% is an appropriate first step for producing the proposed heterogeneous structure.
Partial recrystallization at 750–873 K for 10 minutes to 1 hour followed by water quenching can create the proposed heterogeneous grain structure.
The processing route produces nanometer-to-micrometer grains alongside retained coarse, non-recrystallized grains.
The expected tensile response applies at 293–298 K and strain rates of 5 × 10^-4 to 1 × 10^-3 s^-1.
Processing in argon is required to prevent oxidation.
The relevant mediator is a three-level heterogeneous grain structure spanning nanometer-to-micrometer length scales.
Interfaces between ultrafine and coarse grains generate geometrically necessary dislocations and back stresses.
Coarse grains provide sufficient space for room-temperature deformation twinning and associated strain hardening.
Strain incompatibility between soft coarse grains and hard ultrafine grains induces significant back-stress hardening.
Back-stress hardening accounts for more than 80% of the stress elevation.
Deformation twinning delays necking and enhances uniform elongation.
The ultrafine-grained component supplies the high yield strength.
The heterogeneous alloy will achieve a yield strength above 1000 MPa and uniform elongation above 20% at room temperature.
The heterogeneous alloy will significantly outperform both homogeneous ultrafine-grained material in ductility and coarse-grained material in strength.
A fully recrystallized ultrafine-grained control produced by annealing at 900–1000 °C has approximately 2% uniform strain because twinning is suppressed and strain-hardening capacity is limited.
The strategy is applicable to FCC or metastable FCC alloys whose stacking-fault energy permits deformation twinning.
The strategy may fail in alloys that favor martensitic transformation over twinning or contain brittle intermetallic phases that cannot be homogenized.

contradictions.description: The target structure is called bimodal in the main hypothesis but three-level in the structural-mediator field; these are not necessarily equivalent microstructural classifications.

The intervention describes retained coarse grains as non-recrystallized, whereas the mechanism treats the coarse grains as the soft constituent and the ultrafine grains as the hard constituent. Retained cold-worked non-recrystallized grains would not automatically be the soft population.
